lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: The 110 is open again. I heard a dog fixed it. I don't ask questions.
lines.script: [dry, matter-of-fact] The 110 is open again. I heard a dog fixed it. [deadpan] I don't ask questions.

lines.speaker: Sol
lines.text: LAX. The short way is open. A squirrel ran across the 110 this morning and didn't charge me a toll. First time all week.
lines.script: [easygoing] LAX. The short way is open. [amused, dry] A squirrel ran across the 110 this morning and didn't charge me a toll. [wry] First time all week.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Bready Mercury is in his crock, the crown fits, and the heel goes on your back fence on Saturday. A deal is a deal.
lines.script: [warm, firm] Bready Mercury is in his crock, the crown fits, and the heel goes on your back fence on Saturday. [fond, matter-of-fact] A deal is a DEAL.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: He was a Chairman, babe. You don't stiff a Chairman.
lines.script: [easy, affectionate] [punchline] He was a CHAIRMAN, babe. [warm] You don't stiff a Chairman.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: And call me if it gets spooky. A library that whispers is how at least four horror movies start.
lines.script: [lightly teasing] And call me if it gets spooky. [mock-ominous] A library that whispers is how at least FOUR horror movies start.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Four good ones.
lines.script: [deadpan, fond] Four GOOD ones.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: Go. See this one with your own eyes. I'll feed him fifty and fifty, and I'll sing.
lines.script: [tender, encouraging] Go. See this one with your own EYES. [easy, fond] I'll feed him fifty and fifty, and I'll sing.

lines.speaker: TNB
lines.text: She'll be on your porch when you get home. She always is.
lines.script: [confident, fond] She'll be on your porch when you get home. [warm] She always is.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You're keeping my deal with a squirrel!
lines.script: [outraged, delighted] You're keeping my deal with a SQUIRREL!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Only four?
lines.script: [curious, eager] Only FOUR?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: One throw. Then I have a plane to catch.
lines.script: [fond, hurried] One throw. [firm, cheerful] Then I have a plane to catch.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: He made a crown for a jar of flour and water. I'm keeping him.
lines.script: [fond, amused] He made a crown for a jar of flour and water. [affectionate] I'm keeping him.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Six hours. Then I find out what a library says when it thinks nobody is listening.
lines.script: [eager, curious] Six hours. [dry, anticipating] Then I find out what a library says when it thinks nobody is LISTENING.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you. Lovely flying.
lines.script: [grateful, sincere, soft] Thank you. [warm, proud] Lovely FLYING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata! You came home! The library is still whispering. ALL the books at once, and they're telling everybody's SECRETS.
lines.script: [breathless, excited] Tata! You came HOME! [urgent] The library is still whispering. [outraged] ALL the books at once, and they're telling everybody's SECRETS.

lines.speaker: Whispers
lines.text: ...psst... the uncle is back... psst... he says thank you to the airplane when he gets off...
lines.script: [sly, hushed whisper] ...psst... the uncle is BACK... psst... [giggly, hushed whisper] he says thank you to the AIRPLANE when he gets off...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I heard that from all the way over HERE! And it's true! I do thank the airplane!
lines.script: [shouting, proud] I heard that from all the way over HERE! [delighted, proud] And it's true! I DO thank the airplane!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, that's not how airplanes work. They can't hear you.
lines.script: [patient, matter-of-fact] Tata, that's not how AIRPLANES work. [firm] They can't hear you.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It carried me all the way home, Grace. I'm not going to just walk off.
lines.script: [earnest, warm] It carried me all the way HOME, Grace. [sincere] I'm not going to just WALK OFF.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I say thank you to the bathtub.
lines.script: [proud, loud, matter-of-fact] I say thank you to the BATHTUB.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: See? Rose gets it.
lines.script: [thrilled] See? Rose GETS it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Then we're going in together. I watched the last three on a phone. I'm seeing this one in person.
lines.script: [determined, warm] Then we're going in TOGETHER. [wistful, resolved] I watched the last three on a phone. [firm] I'm seeing this one in PERSON.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Good, because I made the bigger chart. It has six rows, and I left room for seven. A library doesn't whisper for no reason, Tata.
lines.script: [brisk, proud] Good, because I made the BIGGER chart. [bossy, precise] It has six rows, and I left room for SEVEN. [serious] A library doesn't whisper for no REASON, Tata.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Help! I'm stuck in Los ANGELES!
lines.script: [muffled, panicked, yelling] Help! [punchline, shouting] I'm stuck in Los ANGELES!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Don't wrinkle row SIX!
lines.script: [alarmed, bossy] Don't wrinkle row SIX!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: First stop is Deedee's. I've got three burnt bulbs for her drawer, and she's waiting for them.
lines.script: [brisk, cheerful] First stop is Deedee's. [warm] I've got three burnt bulbs for her drawer, and she's waiting for THEM.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: My favorite son! The drawer is open. Hand them over.
lines.script: [warm, commanding] My favorite SON! [brisk] The drawer is open. Hand them OVER.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: The movie studio, the kickball field and the picnic table. The last one came in a sandwich bag, Mom. It was evidence.
lines.script: [earnest, proud] The movie studio, the kickball field and the picnic table. [defensive, pleading] The last one came in a sandwich bag, Mom. It was EVIDENCE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Six, and every one the same. Sit down. Did you eat?
lines.script: [brisk, sharp] Six, and every one the same. [commanding] Sit down. [stern, caring] Did you EAT?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: On the plane. Twice.
lines.script: [sheepish, proud] On the plane. [hopeful] TWICE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's not eating. That's a tray.
lines.script: [flat, withering] [punchline] That's not EATING. That's a TRAY.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Gracie, my crisp is under there.
lines.script: [mild, plaintive] Gracie, my crisp is under THERE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Your crisp is under California, Boppy. Don't move. I'm presenting.
lines.script: [crisp, presenting, unbothered] Your crisp is under CALIFORNIA, Boppy. [firm] Don't move. [grand] I'm PRESENTING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Row one, the dragonfly. A flash. A grey patch. An orange block. A round hole. A burnt bulb. And something that woke up, holding a gold coin.
lines.script: [presenting, ticking off] Row one, the dragonfly. A flash. A grey patch. An orange block. A round hole. A burnt bulb. [building] And something that woke up, holding a gold COIN.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Row two, the lemon. Row three, the fish. Row four, the hat. Row five, the kickball. Row six, the picnic basket. Every row has the same six boxes, and every box is checked.
lines.script: [presenting, quick] Row two, the lemon. Row three, the fish. Row four, the hat. Row five, the kickball. Row six, the picnic basket. [triumphant] Every row has the same six boxes, and every box is CHECKED.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's not six strange things. It's ONE strange thing, six times.
lines.script: [hushed, dramatic] It's not six strange things. [slow, awed] It's ONE strange thing, six times.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: And the coin is the money for the gumball machine.
lines.script: [cheerful, loud] And the coin is the money for the GUMBALL MACHINE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And every block is bigger than the one before. A plum, a grapefruit, a watermelon, a beach ball, a washing machine, a bathtub.
lines.script: [brisk, ticking off] And every block is BIGGER than the one before. [listing] A plum, a grapefruit, a watermelon, a beach ball, a washing machine, a bathtub.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: My fish was no watermelon. Put down rowboat.
lines.script: [indignant, proud] My fish was no watermelon. [grand, dry] Put down ROWBOAT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The BLOCK was a watermelon, Boppy. That's not how charts work. You can't make it bigger because you want to.
lines.script: [firm, exasperated] The BLOCK was a watermelon, Boppy. [stern, patient] That's not how charts work. You can't make it bigger because you WANT to.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Then put a star next to it.
lines.script: [sly, cheerful] Then put a STAR next to it.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I did. The star means "Boppy says it was bigger." It's in the key.
lines.script: [crisp, satisfied] I did. [matter-of-fact] The star means "Boppy says it was bigger." [proud] It's in the KEY.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: There are a LOT of stars.
lines.script: [wide-eyed, delighted] There are a LOT of stars.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Now look at the last column. It says WHERE. Long Island. Los Angeles. Long Island. Los Angeles. Long Island. Los Angeles.
lines.script: [brisk] Now look at the last column. It says WHERE. [slow, ticking off] Long Island. Los Angeles. Long Island. Los Angeles. Long Island. Los Angeles.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It goes back and forth.
lines.script: [dawning, quiet] It goes back and FORTH.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It goes back and forth. Like YOU, Tata.
lines.script: [pointed, matter-of-fact] It goes back and forth. [deadpan] Like YOU, Tata.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Is it Tata?
lines.script: [innocent, curious] Is it TATA?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's not me! I have boarding passes! I kept every single one!
lines.script: [panicked, indignant] It's not me! [proud, pleading] I have BOARDING PASSES! I kept every single ONE!

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Nobody thinks it's you, Tom. Whoever it is leaves their bulbs on the ground. You've never left anything on the ground in your life.
lines.script: [firm, kind] Nobody thinks it's you, Tom. [dry, sharp] Whoever it is leaves their bulbs on the ground. You've never left anything on the ground in your LIFE.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: He cleaned up at his own birthday party. During the party.
lines.script: [amused, proud] He cleaned up at his own BIRTHDAY PARTY. [flat] During the PARTY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It was a nice party! I wanted it to stay nice!
lines.script: [defensive, earnest] It was a NICE party! I wanted it to STAY nice!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: So row seven is on Long Island. And the library started whispering on Monday night. So I filled row seven in already.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, brisk] So row seven is on Long Island. And the library started whispering on Monday night. [satisfied] So I filled row seven in ALREADY.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: A flash. A grey patch. An orange block that's bigger than a bathtub. A round hole. A burnt bulb. And something that woke up, with a gold coin that has a book on it.
lines.script: [reciting, calm] A flash. A grey patch. An orange block that's bigger than a bathtub. A round hole. A burnt bulb. [building] And something that woke up, with a gold coin that has a BOOK on it.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You filled it in before we've even been there?
lines.script: [amazed] You filled it in before we've even BEEN there?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: In pencil. I'll go over it in pen when I'm right.
lines.script: [serene] In PENCIL. [smug] I'll go over it in PEN when I'm right.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: What's this one down here? "MY MEET. TATA COMES."
lines.script: [curious, reading] What's this one down here? [reading aloud, careful] "MY MEET. TATA COMES."

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's not a clue. That's a reminder.
lines.script: [quick, matter-of-fact] That's not a CLUE. [soft, firm] That's a REMINDER.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'll be there.
lines.script: [quiet, sincere] I'll be there.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I know. It's in pen.
lines.script: [quiet, certain] I know. [calm] It's in PEN.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Seven times, on two sides of the country. I want to know who is doing it. And I want to know who raised them, because they can't pick up after themselves.
lines.script: [firm, angry] Seven times, on two sides of the country. I want to know who is doing it. [dry, sharp] And I want to know who RAISED them, because they can't pick up after themselves.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A flash and no thunder. I saw one of those once. The night the meteor came down. Big as a Buick.
lines.script: [reminiscing, grand] A flash and no thunder. I saw one of those once. [booming] The night the meteor came down. [proud] Big as a BUICK.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It was a pebble. It went through the roof of Penny's shop.
lines.script: [flat, patient] It was a PEBBLE. It went through the roof of Penny's shop.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: A Buick-sized pebble.
lines.script: [dignified] A Buick-sized PEBBLE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Should I put the meteor on the chart?
lines.script: [brisk, businesslike] Should I put the meteor on the CHART?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Put it in the key. Under the star.
lines.script: [dry, decisive] Put it in the KEY. [flat] Under the STAR.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Dad, are you coming to the library?
lines.script: [curious, hopeful] Dad, are you coming to the LIBRARY?

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'm not setting one foot in that library. It knows things.
lines.script: [firm, wary] I'm not setting one foot in that library. [dark, hushed] It KNOWS things.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: The cookies in the car? I've been vacuuming that car since before Tom was born, hubby. I didn't need a book to tell me.
lines.script: [dry, sharp] The cookies in the car? I've been vacuuming that car since before Tom was BORN, hubby. [flat] I didn't need a BOOK to tell me.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: ...What else does it know?
lines.script: [small, worried] ...What ELSE does it know?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Go and find out.
lines.script: [brisk, flat] Go and find OUT.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: I'll stay here and guard the crisp, Deary.
lines.script: [dignified, relieved] I'll stay here and guard the crisp, DEARY.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: You three stay together. Nobody goes anywhere alone. And Tom, this time you see it with your own eyes.
lines.script: [firm, loving] You three stay together. Nobody goes anywhere ALONE. [warm, firm] And Tom, this time you see it with your own EYES.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's why I came home, Mom.
lines.script: [warm, simple] That's why I came HOME, Mom.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: One more thing. If a book down there says one word about my pie crust, you didn't hear it.
lines.script: [low, urgent] One more thing. [warning] If a book down there says one word about my pie crust, you didn't HEAR it.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: What about your pie crust?
lines.script: [curious, loud] What about your pie CRUST?

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: NOTHING about my pie crust. Go.
lines.script: [sharp, immediate] NOTHING about my pie crust. [brisk] GO.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: ...It's not fine. It started on Monday night, and it's coming up from the Stacks, the old part of the library downstairs.
lines.script: [hushed, resigned] ...It's not fine. [low, confiding] It started on Monday night, and it's coming up from the Stacks, the old part of the library downstairs.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Books can HEAR? Oh no. I argue with my cookbooks!
lines.script: [appalled, whispering] Books can HEAR? Oh no. [stricken, earnest] I ARGUE with my cookbooks!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Page, on Monday night, was there a big flash?
lines.script: [crisp, suspicious] Page, on Monday night, was there a big FLASH?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: ...How do you know about the flash?
lines.script: [startled, hushed] ...How do you know about the FLASH?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's on my chart. Is there a spot down there where all the color is gone?
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, brisk] It's on my chart. Is there a spot down there where all the color is GONE?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Who TOLD you?
lines.script: [alarmed, hushed] Who TOLD you?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Nobody told me. It's row seven. And is there a big orange block? Bigger than a bathtub?
lines.script: [patient, brisk] Nobody told me. It's row SEVEN. [pointed] And is there a big orange block? Bigger than a BATHTUB?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: My returns cart is inside it. I put a sheet over it. And a sign.
lines.script: [defeated, hushed] My returns cart is INSIDE it. [embarrassed] I put a sheet over it. And a SIGN.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: What does the sign say?
lines.script: [curious] What does the sign SAY?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: "WET FLOOR." It was the only sign I had.
lines.script: [flat, mortified] "WET FLOOR." [small, defensive] It was the only sign I HAD.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And did you find a little burnt bulb on the floor?
lines.script: [quick, probing] And did you find a little burnt BULB on the floor?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: I catalogued it. It's in the card catalog under B. "Bulb, burnt, origin unknown."
lines.script: [stiff, dignified] I CATALOGUED it. [formal] It's in the card catalog under B. "Bulb, burnt, origin unknown."

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Technically correct.
lines.script: [satisfied, crisp] [punchline] Technically CORRECT.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Deeply concerning.
lines.script: [gravely, hushed] DEEPLY concerning.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Page, why did you tell everybody it was fine?
lines.script: [puzzled, gentle] Page, why did you tell everybody it was FINE?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Because a library that isn't quiet gets closed. And then nobody reads ANY of them.
lines.script: [quiet, heartfelt] Because a library that isn't quiet gets CLOSED. [sad] And then nobody reads ANY of them.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I do talk to my bread! He's a very good listener.
lines.script: [proud, fond] I DO talk to my bread! He's a very good LISTENER.

lines.speaker: Whispers
lines.text: ...psst... he sings to it too...
lines.script: [sly, hushed whisper] ...psst... he SINGS to it too...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: That's TNB! If you're going to gossip, get it right!
lines.script: [outraged, delighted] That's TNB! If you're going to gossip, get it RIGHT!

lines.speaker: Whispers
lines.text: ...psst... the small one... psst... she has a secret...
lines.script: [sly, hushed whisper] ...psst... the SMALL one... psst... she has a SECRET...

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I ATE the cookie dough! And I jumped on Boppy's chair! And I moved Grace's bookmark!
lines.script: [shouting, gleeful] I ATE the cookie dough! And I jumped on Boppy's CHAIR! And I moved Grace's BOOKMARK!

lines.speaker: Whispers
lines.text: ...psst... never mind... she tells everybody everything...
lines.script: [defeated, hushed whisper] ...psst... never MIND... she tells everybody EVERYTHING...

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I don't HAVE secrets. I'm too loud.
lines.script: [proud, loud] I don't HAVE secrets. [cheerful] I'm too LOUD.

lines.speaker: Whispers
lines.text: ...psst... Deedee's pie crust... psst... it comes from...
lines.script: [sly, hushed whisper] ...psst... Deedee's pie CRUST... psst... it comes FROM...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: LA la la la LA! I can't hear you! I promised my mother!
lines.script: [panicked, singing over it] LA la la la LA! I can't HEAR you! [shouting] I promised my MOTHER!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Is it over?
lines.script: [muffled, uncertain] Is it OVER?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: WHAT?
lines.script: [muffled, shouting] WHAT?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The floor is grey. That's box two.
lines.script: [quick, checking] The floor is grey. That's box TWO.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's an orange block as big as a golf cart! And there's a whole book cart inside it!
lines.script: [astonished] It's an orange block as big as a golf cart! And there's a whole book cart INSIDE it!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: The books are FALLING OFF! And they're stuck in the air!
lines.script: [shouting, thrilled] The books are FALLING OFF! And they're STUCK in the air!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Bigger than a bathtub. Check.
lines.script: [crisp, satisfied] Bigger than a bathtub. CHECK.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And there's the round hole. Check. It's exactly as big as a coin.
lines.script: [pointing, brisk] And there's the round hole. CHECK. [precise] It's exactly as big as a coin.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You got every box right, and you did it at Deedee's kitchen table.
lines.script: [awed, warm] You got every box right, and you did it at Deedee's kitchen TABLE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'm going over it in pen.
lines.script: [calm, proud] I'm going over it in PEN.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: These books aren't whispering.
lines.script: [whispering, puzzled] These books aren't WHISPERING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The grey ones are quiet. It's the only quiet spot down here.
lines.script: [hushed, working it out] The grey ones are quiet. It's the only quiet spot down HERE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's the only part of the library that still works like a library.
lines.script: [hushed, wry] It's the only part of the library that still works like a LIBRARY.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I want to ride that cart.
lines.script: [eager, loud] I want to RIDE that cart.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Rose. It's in a block.
lines.script: [firm, patient] Rose. It's in a BLOCK.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: After.
lines.script: [unbothered, cheerful] AFTER.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: When we put the coin in, will the books stop talking?
lines.script: [curious, loud] When we put the coin in, will the books stop TALKING?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Everything that woke up goes back to the way it was, Rose. The big squirrel couldn't talk at all afterwards.
lines.script: [brisk, patient] Everything that woke up goes back to the way it was, Rose. [soft, plain] The big squirrel couldn't talk at all AFTERWARDS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: If you can guess all of it before we get here, then it's no accident. Somebody stood right here on Monday night, in my nieces' library.
lines.script: [low, grave] If you can guess all of it before we get here, then it's no accident. [serious] Somebody stood right here on Monday night, in my nieces' LIBRARY.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And they didn't even take out a book.
lines.script: [quiet, dry] And they didn't even take out a BOOK.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: The last box on row seven is something that woke up, with a coin. I bet it's behind those doors.
lines.script: [brisk, confident] The last box on row seven is something that woke up, with a coin. I bet it's behind those DOORS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Something in each of these sections must know a piece of the password. We'll ask nicely first. Then we'll ask nicely again, but louder.
lines.script: [warm, mock-serious] Something in each of these sections must know a piece of the password. We'll ask nicely first. [dry, determined] Then we'll ask nicely again, but LOUDER.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Louder? In a LIBRARY?
lines.script: [scandalized, whispering] LOUDER? In a LIBRARY?

lines.speaker: A picture book
lines.text: ...again?
lines.script: [tiny, hopeful] ...AGAIN?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: What did I see? Tell me! I love a twist!
lines.script: [delighted, eager] What did I see? TELL me! I love a TWIST!

lines.speaker: The Cliffhanger
lines.text: And his mother's favorite child... has always, ALWAYS been...
lines.script: [theatrical, ominous] And his mother's favorite child... [hushed, drawn out] has always, ALWAYS been...

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Been WHO? Me or Amy? Say it!
lines.script: [desperate, thrilled] Been WHO? Me or Amy? SAY it!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I don't know, Cozy Rosie! And I don't know who Deedee's favorite is! This is worse than a season finale!
lines.script: [anguished, comic] I don't know, Cozy Rosie! And I don't know who Deedee's favorite is! [wailing] This is worse than a season FINALE!

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: Actually, Los Angeles is two thousand four hundred and seventy-five miles away. Everybody says three thousand. Actually.
lines.script: [smug, superior] Actually, Los Angeles is two thousand four hundred and seventy-five MILES away. Everybody says three THOUSAND. ACTUALLY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: THANK you! Finally, somebody else is counting!
lines.script: [overjoyed, relieved] THANK you! Finally, somebody else is COUNTING!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Now it sounds like Tata.
lines.script: [flat, matter-of-fact] Now it sounds like TATA.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: ...It does. Grace, it sounds like BOTH of us.
lines.script: [stunned, quiet] ...It does. [amazed] Grace, it sounds like BOTH of us.

lines.speaker: The Know-It-All
lines.text: Actually, the password is none of your business. Actually.
lines.script: [prissy, nasal] Actually, the password is none of your BUSINESS. ACTUALLY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You know a lot, and you tell people. So do I. You got it from me, and I got it from Deedee.
lines.script: [warm, sincere] You know a lot, and you tell people. [fond] So do I. You got it from me, and I got it from DEEDEE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: But that book never asked us one single question. We ask. That's why you're in charge of the signs down here.
lines.script: [warm, steady] But that book never asked us one single QUESTION. [encouraging] We ASK. That's why you're in charge of the signs down HERE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ...Okay. I can work on the asking part. A little. Starting tomorrow.
lines.script: [thoughtful, honest] ...Okay. I can work on the ASKING part. [determined] A little. Starting TOMORROW.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: S. H. H. ...Shh! The password is SHH!
lines.script: [delighted, loud] S. H. H. ...SHH! [triumphant, shouting] The password is SHH!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I was about to say that.
lines.script: [crisp, huffy] I was about to SAY that.

lines.speaker: A dry old voice
lines.text: ...Who's there?
lines.script: [ancient, dry, slow] ...Who's THERE?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's as big as a SUITCASE! And it has an EYE!
lines.script: [awed, loud] It's as big as a SUITCASE! And it has an EYE!

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Excuse me, sir. Are you the one who told the whole Square that I thank the airplane?
lines.script: [polite, wary, earnest] Excuse me, SIR. Are you the one who told the whole Square that I thank the AIRPLANE?

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: You do. Every single time. I think it's lovely. That's why I told everybody.
lines.script: [ancient, dry, fond] You do. Every single TIME. [warm, aching] I think it's LOVELY. That's why I told EVERYBODY.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: On Monday night there was a flash out in the hall. For seventy years I had nothing to say it with. Now I do.
lines.script: [ancient, slow, wistful] On Monday night there was a flash out in the hall. [aching] For seventy years I had nothing to say it with. [quiet, wondering] Now I DO.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And what's your name? Your cover doesn't say anything. It only says "VOLUME ONE."
lines.script: [crisp, bossy] And what's your NAME? Your cover doesn't say anything. [pointed] It only says "VOLUME ONE."

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Volume one of what? I don't know either. Nobody ever opened me to find out.
lines.script: [ancient, bewildered, small] Volume one of WHAT? I don't know either. [bleak, small] Nobody ever opened me to find OUT.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: You don't have a picture on the front. That's why.
lines.script: [matter-of-fact, loud] You don't have a PICTURE on the front. [certain] That's WHY.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: ...Is THAT why?
lines.script: [ancient, stunned, slow] ...Is THAT why?

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. Gold, between the pages. That's my last box.
lines.script: [whispering, urgent] Tata. Gold, between the PAGES. [fierce, quiet] That's my last BOX.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: I talked for four days, and nobody came to listen. Maybe the quiet ones get read.
lines.script: [ancient, bleak, small] I talked for four days, and nobody came to LISTEN. [quiet, wondering] Maybe the quiet ones get READ.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There was a dragon in you the whole time, and nobody knew!
lines.script: [wondering, delighted] There was a dragon in you the whole TIME, and nobody KNEW!

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Neither did I. I only know chapter one. That's as far as anybody has ever read.
lines.script: [ancient, quiet, wondering] Neither did I. [soft, small] I only know chapter one. That's as far as anybody has ever READ.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: There's the coin! He's using it for a bookmark.
lines.script: [quick, thrilled] There's the coin! He's using it for a BOOKMARK.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: The little books brought it to me on Monday night. It's the first bookmark I ever had. You don't need one until somebody opens you.
lines.script: [ancient, gentle] The little books brought it to me on Monday night. It's the first bookmark I ever HAD. [wry, soft] You don't need one until somebody opens YOU.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: It's a book CART. I wrote down "a book." I'm giving myself half a point.
lines.script: [crisp, rueful] It's a book CART. I wrote down "a book." [dry, fair] I'm giving myself HALF a point.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Grace, wait. He should know what it does first.
lines.script: [gentle, firm] Grace, WAIT. [serious, kind] He should know what it does FIRST.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Sir, that coin opens the orange block in the hall. When it does, everything that woke up on Monday night goes back to the way it was. The last one was a squirrel. He couldn't talk afterwards.
lines.script: [gentle, serious, honest] Sir, that coin opens the orange block in the hall. When it does, everything that woke up on Monday night goes back to the way it was. [quiet, careful] The last one was a squirrel. He couldn't talk AFTERWARDS.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: I know. I heard the one in charge explain it out in the hall. Books overhear everything.
lines.script: [ancient, calm] I KNOW. I heard the one in charge explain it out in the hall. [dry, wry] Books overhear EVERYTHING.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: I talked for four days, and everybody covered their ears. You read to me for five minutes, and it was the best day I ever had.
lines.script: [ancient, thoughtful, slow] I talked for four days, and everybody covered their EARS. [warm, aching] You read to me for five minutes, and it was the best day I ever HAD.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: A book isn't supposed to talk. A book is supposed to be READ. So take the coin. But I have conditions.
lines.script: [ancient, gentle, resolved] A book isn't supposed to TALK. A book is supposed to be READ. [dry, warm] So take the coin. But I have CONDITIONS.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I LOVE conditions.
lines.script: [thrilled, bossy] I LOVE conditions.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: One. Somebody reads the rest of me. All of it. Out loud.
lines.script: [ancient, formal] ONE. Somebody reads the rest of me. All of it. Out LOUD.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Me. Saturdays. I'll do every voice.
lines.script: [eager, certain] ME. Saturdays. I'll do every VOICE.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Two. The small loud one is always the dragon.
lines.script: [ancient, formal] TWO. The small loud one is always the DRAGON.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I was ALREADY always the dragon.
lines.script: [indignant, loud] I was ALREADY always the dragon.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Three. I've only just got a place, and I'd hate to lose it. I'm going to need a new bookmark.
lines.script: [ancient, formal, wistful] THREE. I've only just got a place, and I'd hate to LOSE it. I'm going to need a new BOOKMARK.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You can have mine. I bedazzled it myself.
lines.script: [shy, proud] You can have MINE. I bedazzled it MYSELF.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: It says, "THIS IS GRACE'S PAGE. DO NOT MOVE IT. THIS MEANS YOU, ROSE."
lines.script: [ancient, reading, slow] It says, "THIS IS GRACE'S PAGE. DO NOT MOVE IT. THIS MEANS YOU, ROSE."

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I only moved it ONE time!
lines.script: [defensive, loud] I only moved it ONE time!

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You moved it twice. It's in my notebook.
lines.script: [flat, certain] You moved it TWICE. It's in my NOTEBOOK.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: It's the most beautiful thing anybody has ever put in me.
lines.script: [ancient, moved, slow] It's the most beautiful thing anybody has ever put in ME.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: And four. Carry me out to the hall. I've never seen how anything ends.
lines.script: [ancient, formal, wistful] And FOUR. Carry me out to the hall. [quiet, wondering] I've never seen how anything ENDS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It would be an honor, sir. I'm going to lift you by the spine. Is that all right?
lines.script: [solemn, honored] It would be an honor, SIR. [careful, polite] I'm going to lift you by the spine. Is that all RIGHT?

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Mind the corners. They're seventy.
lines.script: [ancient, dry, prim] Mind the CORNERS. They're SEVENTY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: You're heavier than you look.
lines.script: [strained, comic] You're HEAVIER than you look.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: It's the dust.
lines.script: [ancient, dry, deadpan] It's the DUST.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Higher. I can't see over the globe.
lines.script: [ancient, dry, impatient] HIGHER. I can't see over the GLOBE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: First I held a net. Then I held a binder. Now I'm a lectern! I keep getting promoted!
lines.script: [strained, joyful, proud] First I held a net. Then I held a binder. Now I'm a LECTERN! [punchline, delighted] I keep getting PROMOTED!

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Is that the Reading Room book? It hasn't left that room since 1952!
lines.script: [stunned, hushed] Is that the Reading Room book? It hasn't left that room since 1952!

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: Hello, Page. You hum in the elevator.
lines.script: [ancient, dry, friendly] Hello, Page. [deadpan] You hum in the ELEVATOR.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: ...Everything is fine.
lines.script: [stiff, mortified, hushed] ...Everything is FINE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Thirteen.
lines.script: [flat, counting] THIRTEEN.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata. If I put it in, he stops.
lines.script: [small, serious] Tata. If I put it in, he STOPS.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I know. He knows too. I'm right here.
lines.script: [gentle, steady] I know. He knows TOO. [warm] I'm right HERE.

lines.speaker: The Unread
lines.text: You're the one in charge, aren't you? Go on, then. Turn the page.
lines.script: [ancient, kind, dry] You're the one in charge, aren't you? Go on, then. [warm, slow] Turn the PAGE.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Tata. He stopped.
lines.script: [whispering, small] Tata. He STOPPED.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: He didn't stop, Rose. He's on page twelve. He's waiting for Saturday.
lines.script: [soft, steady] He didn't stop, Rose. He's on page TWELVE. [warm] He's waiting for SATURDAY.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Thank you, sir.
lines.script: [soft, sincere] Thank you, SIR.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, he can't hear you anymore.
lines.script: [gentle, matter-of-fact] Tata, he can't hear you ANYMORE.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Neither can the airplane.
lines.script: [soft, wry, tender] [punchline] Neither can the AIRPLANE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: ...Thank you, sir.
lines.script: [quiet, soft] ...Thank you, SIR.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: THANK YOU, BOOK!
lines.script: [shouting, cheerful] THANK YOU, BOOK!

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Shhh.
lines.script: [hushed, firm] SHHH.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: Thank you, book.
lines.script: [whispering, cheerful] Thank you, BOOK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I saw it. All of it, from right here. Not on a phone.
lines.script: [quiet, amazed] I SAW it. All of it, from right here. [warm, proud] Not on a PHONE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: You were standing in the way of the cart.
lines.script: [crisp, dry] You were standing in the way of the CART.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I had the best seat in the house!
lines.script: [delighted, proud] I had the best seat in the HOUSE!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's AFTER. Push me!
lines.script: [shouting, gleeful] It's AFTER. [bossy] PUSH me!

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: That cart is for returns only.
lines.script: [stiff, prim, hushed] That cart is for returns ONLY.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: I'm RETURNING. I'm returning upstairs.
lines.script: [indignant, loud] I'm RETURNING. [triumphant] I'm returning UPSTAIRS.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: That's not how returns work.
lines.script: [crisp, flat] That's not how RETURNS work.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's a little bit how returns work.
lines.script: [wry, fair] It's a little bit how returns WORK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "To be continued in volume two." Page! Where's volume two?
lines.script: [reading, dismayed] "To be continued in volume two." [alarmed] Page! Where's volume TWO?

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Checked out. In 1998. It was a bad week.
lines.script: [flat, grave, hushed] Checked out. In 1998. [dry, rueful] It was a bad WEEK.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: NO!
lines.script: [anguished, comic] NO!

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: AAAAH! ...Again!
lines.script: [screaming, delighted] AAAAH! [thrilled] ...AGAIN!

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Everything is fine.
lines.script: [gentle, warm, hushed] Everything is FINE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Fourteen. And that's the first one I believe.
lines.script: [crisp, satisfied] FOURTEEN. [warm, honest] And that's the first one I BELIEVE.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: Is it safe? Has it stopped talking?
lines.script: [wary, hushed] Is it safe? Has it stopped TALKING?

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: It's all quiet, Boppy. It can't tell on you anymore.
lines.script: [earnest, loud] It's all quiet, Boppy. [gleeful] It can't tell on you ANYMORE.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: I saw that.
lines.script: [flat, sharp] I SAW that.

lines.speaker: Boppy
lines.text: The books didn't.
lines.script: [mild, serene] [punchline] The BOOKS didn't.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, here's number seven. Page had it filed in the card catalog.
lines.script: [warm, brisk] Mom, here's number SEVEN. Page had it filed in the card CATALOG.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: It's checked out on Grace's card. It's due back in three weeks.
lines.script: [prim, hushed] It's checked out on Grace's card. It's due back in three WEEKS.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: It's going in my drawer, and it's staying in my drawer.
lines.script: [firm, flat] It's going in my drawer, and it's staying in my DRAWER.

lines.speaker: Page
lines.text: Then there will be a late fee.
lines.script: [dry, apologetic] Then there will be a late FEE.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: NO late fees. EVER.
lines.script: [loud, triumphant] NO late fees. EVER.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Tom. Did that library say anything about my pie crust?
lines.script: [sharp, casual, probing] Tom. Did that library say anything about my pie CRUST?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I didn't hear one word, Mom.
lines.script: [innocent, quick] I didn't hear one word, MOM.

lines.speaker: Rose
lines.text: He sang LA LA LA.
lines.script: [loud, helpful] He sang LA LA LA.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: That's my favorite son.
lines.script: [warm, satisfied] That's my favorite SON.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Mom, one of the books knew who your favorite really is.
lines.script: [mischievous, careful] Mom, one of the books knew who your favorite REALLY is.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: And?
lines.script: [sharp, level] And?

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It turned back into a regular book before it told me.
lines.script: [sheepish, amused] It turned back into a regular book before it told ME.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Smart book.
lines.script: [dry, approving] SMART book.

lines.speaker: Deedee
lines.text: Seven bulbs. Somebody was in this library on Monday night, down there with the children's books. I don't like it one bit.
lines.script: [grave, low] Seven bulbs. Somebody was in this library on Monday night, down there with the children's books. [firm, quiet] I don't like it one BIT.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: And the next one is in Los Angeles, Deedee. It goes back and forth.
lines.script: [crisp, certain] And the next one is in Los Angeles, DEEDEE. It goes back and FORTH.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: It's TNB. "Babe. Bernadette signed you up for the 2nd Ave potluck. You're on bread. For forty people."
lines.script: [reading, amused] It's TNB. "Babe. Bernadette signed you up for the 2nd Ave potluck. You're on BREAD. For forty PEOPLE."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: "I said yes for you. You're welcome. Bready and I have already started."
lines.script: [reading, fond] "I said yes for you. You're WELCOME. Bready and I have already STARTED."

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: Forty people! It's a good thing he lives in a crock now.
lines.script: [delighted, thrilled] Forty people! [fond, proud] It's a good thing he lives in a CROCK now.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Tata, row eight is going to be in Los Angeles. I left room.
lines.script: [firm, quiet, certain] Tata, row eight is going to be in Los Angeles. [matter-of-fact] I left ROOM.

lines.speaker: Tom
lines.text: I'll look for every box. And I'll call you before I touch anything.
lines.script: [warm, determined] I'll look for every box. And I'll call you before I touch ANYTHING.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Good. I'm in charge of row eight.
lines.script: [crisp, proud] Good. I'm in charge of row EIGHT.
